structure.heading: Budget-at-Completion Forecast, Dependency Risks, and Steering Committee Escalations
text_content: **Budget-at-Completion Forecast, Dependency Risks, and Steering Committee Escalations**

The programme Budget‑at‑Completion (BAC) forecast is $128.4m versus an approved budget of $125.0m, representing a variance of +$3.4m (+2.7%). This forecasted overrun is concentrated in recently validated vendor estimates and higher-than-expected licensing and compliance costs for the current phase. The finance team has applied earned value analysis and reforecasted contingencies to produce the $128.4m figure; contingency burn to date is 62% of plan. Management will continue to monitor spend profiles monthly and will seek cost offsets where feasible, but at present the BAC impact requires recognition in the programme portfolio and tracking against corporate risk appetite. Senior stakeholders have been briefed and monthly forecast revisions will be reported to the Steering Committee.

The Systems Integrator forecasted Estimate at Completion (EAC) is $46.2m against a budget of $44.0m, producing a variance of +$2.2m attributable to schedule acceleration premiums and additional integration testing scope. The Systems Integrator contract (SI) is under review with procurement and legal to determine entitlement for change orders and to identify immediate opportunities to reduce the gap through scope prioritisation, phasing, and supplier rate moderation. Actions in flight include revised delivery milestones, a targeted value‑engineering workshop week commencing 11 May 2026, and a requirement for the SI to submit a corrective cost plan within ten business days. Executive oversight engaged.

A material dependency and escalation requires immediate Steering Committee attention: a decision is required by 20 May 2026 to approve a $1.8m change request (CR-017) to deliver expanded regulatory reporting scope. CR-017 is critical to meet external reporting deadlines and is linked to upstream data-delivery dependencies from Data Platform and downstream audit sign-off milestones; failure to decide by 20 May 2026 will introduce schedule slippage of up to six weeks and increase programme risk exposure. Recommended options for the Steering Committee are: 1) approve CR-017 for $1.8m and accelerate vendor onboarding; or 2) defer approval and accept the consequent schedule and compliance risk. A decision and recorded action are required.

structure.heading: Milestone Health, Critical Path, and Next-Period Delivery Commitments
text_content: **Milestone Health, Critical Path, and Next-Period Delivery Commitments**

Milestone health review identifies Milestone M4 (Data Platform MVP) as forecast for 14 Jun 2026, representing a 10‑day delay against the baseline date of 04 Jun 2026. This variance places M4 on the programme critical path, increasing scrutiny from the Integration Office and Data Platform team. Milestone M5 (Finance ERP Cutover) remains on track for 30 Sep 2026 with 0 days variance, and therefore does not currently contribute to critical‑path slippage. Updated Gantt and critical‑path diagrams will be published to stakeholders within two working days for executive review promptly.

The programme will prioritise recovery actions to mitigate the M4 slip and preserve the overall delivery timeline. Key next-period commitment: complete SIT Cycle 2 by 24 May 2026, owned by the Testing Directorate and Data Platform team. Recovery measures include: 1. Re-sequencing non‑critical integration tasks to free a two‑week window for platform stabilisation; 2. Short‑term augmentation of two senior engineers and one test lead; 3. Weekend regression runs and daily status gating. Progress against the SIT Cycle 2 completion date will be reported in the weekly Integrated Programme report.

To support delivery in the next reporting period, the Release Management Office will enforce entry and exit criteria for each phase. For M4, exit criteria require successful completion of SIT Cycle 2, resolution of priority‑1 defects, and sign‑off from Data Platform QA and Architecture by the handover date. M5 readiness will continue to be validated against cutover runbooks and reconciliation tests; it remains on track for 30 Sep 2026 with 0 days variance. The PMO will publish a daily RAG dashboard; Change Control Board will review scope adjustments weekly.
